assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production bitmap surface atlas for the Pale Ward retro FPS. Generate a landscape 1536 by 1024 PNG, opaque, EXACT 3 columns by 2 rows of six 512-square panels, no gutters, borders, labels or text. Each panel is a straight-on flat material painting, without perspective or scene objects. Top row left-to-right WALL, FLOOR, CEILING. Bottom row left-to-right TRIM, DOOR, EQUIPMENT PANEL. These names are instructions only, never letters in the image. Every panel independently tiles on all four edges. Art direction matches a gritty 1990s Doom/Quake biotech facility: carefully hand-placed pixel clusters, fine chipped edges, scratches, layered dirt and convincingly dimensional painted material detail; restrained native pixel granularity, no smooth photoreal gradients, no cartoon outline, no grainy random noise blanket. Use subdued brown-gray, charcoal, aged ivory and restrained hospital green, with dark readable recesses. Flat neutral lighting, no baked directional light, no cast shadows, no scene render or mockup. High detail is concentrated at seams, hardware and wear. All six panels fill their cells edge to edge and align to the exact grid. Specific family: EMERGENCY TRIAGE medical ward. Wall: small worn ivory ceramic tiles with dark grout, scattered restrained hairline cracks, a thin desaturated sage-green band, believable washable clinical wall rather than giant bolted concrete slabs. Floor: dark olive-gray non-slip square linoleum/metal composite tiles, accumulated dirt at fine seams, occasional rusty drain lattice integrated flush, sparse dark old stains. Ceiling: aged offwhite acoustic service squares with fine perforations and dark recessed narrow metal seams. Trim: scuffed steel-and-ivory service edging with tiny bolts and chipped green paint. Door: heavy institutional steel face, sage-green worn enamel, narrow recessed metal reinforcement and riveted hardware without signage. Equipment panel: worn cream painted sheet steel, dark vent slits, screws and small inset blank instrument cover. Maintain a cohesive tactile medical-industrial palette; architectural detail must be finer and more varied than a single repeating large four-bolt plate.
